chapter: Building the band: Dave Duncan, Denver and Rene Hall
title: Dorsey books the Denver battle of bands against Smiling Billy Stewart
summary: Phil Dorsey lines up small-town dates and a winner-take-all battle of bands in Colorado; Fields dates it about 1930-32 and talks about a white man in a Black band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And so Dave stayed with us in our home. He had a room there. And then he went to work and then he was with us when Phil Dorsey called and told me he had a few dates and he said I got a date, several little dates in small towns in Kansas and a few in Nebraska, but I've got you in Colorado with a battle of bands with Smiling Billy Stewart. I had never heard about Billy Stewart, and Smiling Billy Stewart at that time had a twelve or fourteen piece band and he said it's going to be a battle of the bands, winner take all. That's the way we're advertising it, but it's going to be a big thing, you
I would say--because Eddie Nicholson was there--it must have been around 1930, approximately; somewhere along in there. Not over thirty one or two, because it was kind of during the depression.
I think people might not understand, it was revolutionary, for a white guy to be with a black band; that was a big thing.

I told him right then you can say you're the manager or anything and he said I understand, and he was a very fine fellow and a good musician and the only thing after he finally left the band, Spurgeons said, I'll tell you one thing--
(Side B of Tape 1 ended at this point. Transcript will continue with Tape 2.)
